classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the two starting populations, calculate transfers relative to each group and combine the resulting employed proportions.

content.prompt: In a particular country in 2011, $12\%$ of the population was unemployed and $88\%$ was employed. In 2012, $10\%$ of the unemployed people became employed and $10\%$ of those employed became unemployed. What percentage of the population was employed at the end of 2012?

answer.short:
$80.4\%$.

Retain $90\%$ of the originally employed group and add $10\%$ of the originally unemployed group.
answer.worked:
The percentages transferred are calculated from the two original groups.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Originally employed who remain employed}&=88\%\times0.90\\\text{Originally employed who remain employed}&=79.2\%\\\text{Originally unemployed who become employed}&=12\%\times0.10\\\text{Originally unemployed who become employed}&=1.2\%\\\text{Population employed at the end of 2012}&=79.2\%+1.2\%\\\text{Population employed at the end of 2012}&=80.4\%\end{align*}$$
